hook: I bought a **faulty product** and the company won't fix it.
hook_q: How do I file a consumer complaint?

slides.title: You can **file online.**
slides.body: The Act allows complaints to be filed electronically. On the government's e-Daakhil portal (edaakhil.nic.in) you can file and pay the fee online. It works for the National Commission and all States/UTs.

slides.title: File **where you live.**
slides.body: You can file in the District Commission where you live or work, not only where the seller is based.

slides.title: Which commission? It depends on **what you paid.**
Paid up to ₹5 lakh? **No filing fee.**
slides.body: Complaints where the amount paid for the goods or service is up to ₹5 lakh have no fee.

timeline.text: The **cause of action** arises (e.g., the defect appears or the company refuses to fix it). The 2-year clock starts here.
Last date to file. After that, you must show **sufficient cause** for the delay.

slides.title: Not for **resale or business** purchases.
slides.body: If you bought goods for resale or a commercial purpose, or hired services for a commercial purpose, you're not a "consumer" under the Act. Goods bought and used by you exclusively to earn your livelihood through self-employment are an exception.

sources: CDRC Rules, 2020 – Rule 7, as amended Aug 2023 (e-Gazette)
caption:
Got a faulty product or bad service? Here's how to file a consumer complaint. 👇

1️⃣ File online on e-Daakhil (edaakhil.nic.in), available across all States/UTs
2️⃣ At the District or State Commission, you can file where you live or work
3️⃣ Up to ₹50 lakh: District Commission. ₹50 lakh to ₹2 crore: State. Above ₹2 crore: National
4️⃣ No filing fee if you paid up to ₹5 lakh
5️⃣ File within 2 years from when the cause of action arises

Source: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Sec 2(7), 34, 35, 69); Jurisdiction Rules 2021; CDRC Rules 2020 (as amended 2023); PIB
